concerns.text: Phase 6 introduces 11 tasks (T031-T041) implementing 'Blind Cue', 'Network Topology', 'Forgetting', 'Noise Injection', and 'Scaling Cost' features. These features have NO corresponding Functional Requirements (FR), User Stories (US), or Success Criteria (SC) in spec.md. The spec explicitly limits scope to US-1, US-2, US-3 and FR-001 through FR-012. Implementing Phase 6 without spec authorization creates untraceable work.

Task T022 implements a sensitivity analysis sweeping token limits {128, 256, 512} as required by FR-008. However, Task T018 (Limited-context simulation) and the Plan.md Methodology section define 'Limited' context as a single 'predefined token threshold' without the systematic sweep. There is no task explicitly linking the T022 sweep logic to the T018 execution loop to ensure the sweep is actually performed across the required set.

Task T030 generates `scaling_plot.pdf` and requires a specific verification string. However, the Analyze Report flags this task as 'REJECTED' because the deliverable file is missing. While the task exists in the list, the absence of the actual artifact means Success Criterion SC-005 (generate scaling plot) is currently unfulfilled and unverified.

Tasks T031 and T032 implement a 'Blind Cue' protocol (masking internal context) to distinguish transactive memory from pattern matching. Spec FR-005 and US-1 define cue-retrieval efficiency simply as 'proportion of successful fact-retrieval queries' with no mention of masking or blind conditions. There is no task mapping to a spec requirement that authorizes this logic change, creating a contradiction between implementation and acceptance criteria.

Tasks T033 and T034 implement configurable network topologies (sparse_small_world, ring) and neighbor-only querying. Spec FR-003 and Assumptions describe a 'shared external memory buffer' accessible by all agents with no topological constraints. No spec requirement exists to authorize the implementation of network topology constraints.

Tasks T035 and T036 implement a 'Forgetting Mechanism' with decay rates and consolidation. Spec Assumptions state 'The external memory buffer size will remain within disk usage limits' and describe a standard read/write buffer. No spec requirement exists to authorize decay, probabilistic removal, or time-based expiration logic.

Task T031 is tagged with '(US-1, Turing Review)'. 'Turing Review' is not a valid User Story ID in spec.md (which only lists US-1, US-2, US-3). This is a stale or invalid tag referencing a non-existent requirement ID.
